<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="" spellcheck="false">This collage shows Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan (Left) and party's Information Secretary Shaukat Yousafzai. — National Assembly/Khyber Pakhtunkhwa govt website/File</figcaption><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><sider-quick-compose-btn dir="ltr" data-gpts-theme="light" data-ext-text-inserter="no" style="display: contents;"></sider-quick-compose-btn><superhuman-go-underlines data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; display: contents; --rem: 16;"></superhuman-go-underlines></figure></div><ul><li><b>Gohar rejects reports of dissolving KP Assembly or replacing  KP CM.</b></li><li><b>PTI's Ali Zafar says Oct 4 long march is final and non-negotiable.</b></li><li><b>Law Minister Tarar says government had not refused talks with PTI.</b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>PESHAWAR: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Information Secretary Shaukat Yousafzai has urged the party leadership to further postpone the long march, now scheduled for October 4, warning that the risk of emergency rule made it imperative to delay the protest.</p><p>In the letter addressed to PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar and other party leaders on Tuesday, Yousafzai said the march should be postponed in the wider national interest, particularly given the security situation and increased terrorist activity. </p><style>

	</div><p>He warned that the federal government could use certain issues as a pretext to impose emergency rule, and that a possible attack from Afghanistan could serve as justification for such a move.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">

</div>
<p>He said the federal government was building a narrative that the KP government was not cooperating, and that this could lead to attempts to dissolve the provincial government or accuse the party of supporting terrorism, potentially leading to a ban on PTI. </p><p>He cited PTI founder Imran Khan's own precedent of ending a previous long march to protect workers' lives and urged the leadership to take his concerns seriously. He called for dialogue with the state rather than confrontation.</p><p>The letter comes days after PTI announced that its long march towards Islamabad, originally scheduled for September 27, had been postponed to October 4.</p><p>The former ruling party was preparing for a major protest and march on Islamabad, demanding the release of its jailed founder Imran Khan and the “restoration” of constitutional supremacy.</p><p>Meanwhile, PTI Chairman Gohar rejected the suggestion and reaffirmed the long march decision, saying the party had no intention of dissolving the KP provincial assembly and that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi could not be disqualified under any circumstances. </p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">

		<div class="medium-insert-embed">

	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>He said no consultation had taken place regarding finding an alternative to Afridi and that reports to the contrary were fabricated. He said Afridi had the full confidence of PTI founder Imran Khan and would remain chief minister.</p><h2>Negotiations </h2><p>Separately, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the government had not refused talks with PTI but objected to the party making Imran Khan's release a precondition for dialogue, saying the forum for his release was the courts, not the government. </p><p>He said while legal and constitutional channels existed, PTI wanted to secure the founder's release through rallies, processions and marching on cities, which was not possible. </p><p>On the Supreme Court's order regarding Imran's transfer to a private hospital, Tarar said the court had ordered a medical examination which was completed, and that any shortcomings in implementation were for the court to examine — not for street protests to resolve.</p><p>Meanwhile, PTI Senator Ali Zafar said the postponement of the long march to October 4 now gave the government an opportunity to hold talks, saying if the government took one step, negotiations could begin. </p><p>He said the meeting between the opposition leader and the government before September 27 could not be called negotiations, and that proper talks should be held through committees in closed rooms. He said the October 4 long march was final and that the government was afraid of it.</p><h2>Opposition meets PPP's Nayyar Bukhari</h2><p>Meanwhile, opposition leaders held a meeting with Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Parliamentarians Secretary General Nayyar Bukhari at party's central secretariat in Islamabad, according to a press release issued by Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayn-e-Pakistan. </p><p>The opposition leaders, including Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Senator Zeeshan and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai, invited the PPP to attend an all parties conference. </p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2104887510874620052" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>Addressing the media after the meeting, Bukhari said the opposition had proposed an All Parties Conference and that he had given assurances to speak with the party chairman Bilawal Bhutto.</p><p>Abbas said political parties come together in times of crisis, describing the current moment as difficult and stressing the need for unity and eliminating despondency. </p><p>Gohar said several proposals had been placed before the meeting, that work on an APC was ongoing, that an invitation had been extended by the united opposition and that provincial autonomy was critical in a democracy. </p><p>He reiterated that the long march decision remained intact and that political parties, despite differences, were united for democracy.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v31edd6df95cf4e85bb4c19e7a9bdbcba1788362987495" integrity="sha512-iIg7k2xntmwu6/uSb5tpc/hySgZc4eoL31yB29W6tJFo2akwjPWcEqnCEdJvGexCL0KEQwVYv5BlowfhVz26hg==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

headline: PTI leader urges party to further postpone long march, warns of emergency risk
subheadline: PPP's Nayyar Bukhari welcomes opposition's proposed APC, assures to speak to chairman Bilawal Bhutto
author: Abubakar Saddiq, Web Desk
article_text:
Gohar rejects reports of dissolving KP Assembly or replacing KP CM.
PTI's Ali Zafar says Oct 4 long march is final and non-negotiable.
Law Minister Tarar says government had not refused talks with PTI.

PESHAWAR: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Information Secretary Shaukat Yousafzai has urged the party leadership to further postpone the long march, now scheduled for October 4, warning that the risk of emergency rule made it imperative to delay the protest.

In the letter addressed to PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar and other party leaders on Tuesday, Yousafzai said the march should be postponed in the wider national interest, particularly given the security situation and increased terrorist activity.

He warned that the federal government could use certain issues as a pretext to impose emergency rule, and that a possible attack from Afghanistan could serve as justification for such a move.

He said the federal government was building a narrative that the KP government was not cooperating, and that this could lead to attempts to dissolve the provincial government or accuse the party of supporting terrorism, potentially leading to a ban on PTI.

He cited PTI founder Imran Khan's own precedent of ending a previous long march to protect workers' lives and urged the leadership to take his concerns seriously. He called for dialogue with the state rather than confrontation.

The letter comes days after PTI announced that its long march towards Islamabad, originally scheduled for September 27, had been postponed to October 4.

The former ruling party was preparing for a major protest and march on Islamabad, demanding the release of its jailed founder Imran Khan and the “restoration” of constitutional supremacy.

Meanwhile, PTI Chairman Gohar rejected the suggestion and reaffirmed the long march decision, saying the party had no intention of dissolving the KP provincial assembly and that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi could not be disqualified under any circumstances.

He said no consultation had taken place regarding finding an alternative to Afridi and that reports to the contrary were fabricated. He said Afridi had the full confidence of PTI founder Imran Khan and would remain chief minister.

Negotiations

Separately, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the government had not refused talks with PTI but objected to the party making Imran Khan's release a precondition for dialogue, saying the forum for his release was the courts, not the government.

He said while legal and constitutional channels existed, PTI wanted to secure the founder's release through rallies, processions and marching on cities, which was not possible.

On the Supreme Court's order regarding Imran's transfer to a private hospital, Tarar said the court had ordered a medical examination which was completed, and that any shortcomings in implementation were for the court to examine — not for street protests to resolve.

Meanwhile, PTI Senator Ali Zafar said the postponement of the long march to October 4 now gave the government an opportunity to hold talks, saying if the government took one step, negotiations could begin.

He said the meeting between the opposition leader and the government before September 27 could not be called negotiations, and that proper talks should be held through committees in closed rooms. He said the October 4 long march was final and that the government was afraid of it.

Opposition meets PPP's Nayyar Bukhari

Meanwhile, opposition leaders held a meeting with Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Parliamentarians Secretary General Nayyar Bukhari at party's central secretariat in Islamabad, according to a press release issued by Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayn-e-Pakistan.

The opposition leaders, including Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Senator Zeeshan and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai, invited the PPP to attend an all parties conference.

Addressing the media after the meeting, Bukhari said the opposition had proposed an All Parties Conference and that he had given assurances to speak with the party chairman Bilawal Bhutto.

Abbas said political parties come together in times of crisis, describing the current moment as difficult and stressing the need for unity and eliminating despondency.

Gohar said several proposals had been placed before the meeting, that work on an APC was ongoing, that an invitation had been extended by the united opposition and that provincial autonomy was critical in a democracy.

He reiterated that the long march decision remained intact and that political parties, despite differences, were united for democracy.

• Gohar rejects reports of dissolving KP Assembly or replacing  KP CM.
  • PTI's Ali Zafar says Oct 4 long march is final and non-negotiable.
  • Law Minister Tarar says government had not refused talks with PTI.

PESHAWAR: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Information Secretary Shaukat Yousafzai has urged the party leadership to further postpone the long march, now scheduled for October 4, warning that the risk of emergency rule made it imperative to delay the protest.

In the letter addressed to PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar and other party leaders on Tuesday, Yousafzai said the march should be postponed in the wider national interest, particularly given the security situation and increased terrorist activity.

He warned that the federal government could use certain issues as a pretext to impose emergency rule, and that a possible attack from Afghanistan could serve as justification for such a move.

He said the federal government was building a narrative that the KP government was not cooperating, and that this could lead to attempts to dissolve the provincial government or accuse the party of supporting terrorism, potentially leading to a ban on PTI.

He cited PTI founder Imran Khan's own precedent of ending a previous long march to protect workers' lives and urged the leadership to take his concerns seriously. He called for dialogue with the state rather than confrontation.

The letter comes days after PTI announced that its long march towards Islamabad, originally scheduled for September 27, had been postponed to October 4.

The former ruling party was preparing for a major protest and march on Islamabad, demanding the release of its jailed founder Imran Khan and the “restoration” of constitutional supremacy.

Meanwhile, PTI Chairman Gohar rejected the suggestion and reaffirmed the long march decision, saying the party had no intention of dissolving the KP provincial assembly and that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi could not be disqualified under any circumstances.

He said no consultation had taken place regarding finding an alternative to Afridi and that reports to the contrary were fabricated. He said Afridi had the full confidence of PTI founder Imran Khan and would remain chief minister.

Negotiations

Separately, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the government had not refused talks with PTI but objected to the party making Imran Khan's release a precondition for dialogue, saying the forum for his release was the courts, not the government.

He said while legal and constitutional channels existed, PTI wanted to secure the founder's release through rallies, processions and marching on cities, which was not possible.

On the Supreme Court's order regarding Imran's transfer to a private hospital, Tarar said the court had ordered a medical examination which was completed, and that any shortcomings in implementation were for the court to examine — not for street protests to resolve.

Meanwhile, PTI Senator Ali Zafar said the postponement of the long march to October 4 now gave the government an opportunity to hold talks, saying if the government took one step, negotiations could begin.

He said the meeting between the opposition leader and the government before September 27 could not be called negotiations, and that proper talks should be held through committees in closed rooms. He said the October 4 long march was final and that the government was afraid of it.

Opposition meets PPP's Nayyar Bukhari

Meanwhile, opposition leaders held a meeting with Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Parliamentarians Secretary General Nayyar Bukhari at party's central secretariat in Islamabad, according to a press release issued by Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayn-e-Pakistan.

The opposition leaders, including Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Senator Zeeshan and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai, invited the PPP to attend an all parties conference.

Addressing the media after the meeting, Bukhari said the opposition had proposed an All Parties Conference and that he had given assurances to speak with the party chairman Bilawal Bhutto.

Abbas said political parties come together in times of crisis, describing the current moment as difficult and stressing the need for unity and eliminating despondency.

Gohar said several proposals had been placed before the meeting, that work on an APC was ongoing, that an invitation had been extended by the united opposition and that provincial autonomy was critical in a democracy.

He reiterated that the long march decision remained intact and that political parties, despite differences, were united for democracy.
